known_limitations_and_physics.wind_roughened_water: Sentinel-1 C-band (5.6 cm wavelength) experiences Bragg resonant scattering over wind-rippled river reaches and wide haor fetches during monsoon squalls, raising VV/VH backscatter and causing missed water pixels. NISAR L-band (24 cm wavelength) is less sensitive to capillary ripples.
known_limitations_and_physics.flooded_vegetation_double_bounce: L-band 24 cm microwaves penetrate rice and wetland reed canopies to form a trunk/stalk-water dihedral corner reflector (+2.5 to +7 dB HH rise), whereas C-band 5.6 cm scatters primarily in upper foliage.
known_limitations_and_physics.urban_and_shadow_confusion: Smooth asphalt roads, airstrips, and dry flat sandbars (chars) can exhibit low specular backscatter similar to open water; combining JRC permanent water masks and dual-pol thresholds mitigates false positives.
known_limitations_and_physics.data_maturity: NISAR scenes are calibrated PROVISIONAL products (CRID P05023/P05036) from June 18 to Nov 9, 2026, posted at 80 m (Frequency B) / 10 m (Frequency A) with a 3x3 Lee speckle filter.
